Missing option: Google Play internal app sharing. You upload an APK or AAB signed with any key, debuggable builds allowed, and version codes may be reused. Google re-signs it with an Internal App Sharing key. Each link allows up to 100 downloaders and expires after 60 days. The Play Store installs it, which by Samsung's rule should pass Auto Blocker. It needs a Play Console account but no review or testing-track requirements. Because of the re-signing, it cannot update builds signed with the GitHub key. Source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9844679?hl=en

Option E overstates its setup cost. Play internal testing has 'Requirements to access track: None' and can be used 'before completing your app setup' or for 'apps that are not fully configured', so a store listing and policy forms are not needed to start internal testing. Sources: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14151465?hl=en and https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9845334?hl=en

Option E's 'different key from GitHub builds' can be avoided. For a new app, Play App Signing lets you choose and upload your own app signing key instead of having Google generate one. Play-delivered and GitHub/Obtainium builds can then share one certificate and update each other. Source: https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/app-signing ('or you would like to choose the app signing key for a new app instead of having Google generate it ... Upload your app's signing key to Play App Signing')

Firebase AAB distribution goes through Google Play internal app sharing. Play developers had to register any remaining Play apps by 30 Sep 2026 'to avoid global removal from Google Play'. Sources: https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/google-play-console and https://android-developers.googleblog.com/2026/06/android-developer-verification.html

Scope limits of enforcement. Outside Play, enforcement 'will only apply to mobile and tablet form factors in the selected regions'. Checks do not run in comprehensively sanctioned countries or where Google Mobile Services are unsupported, and AOSP and non-certified devices are exempt. Sources: https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/faq and https://support.google.com/android/answer/17065026?hl=en

Advanced flow practicalities. Switching it off briefly gives a 10-minute grace period without a new 24-hour wait. The flow also governs updates to unregistered apps. The Android Developer Verifier (com.google.android.verifier) can be installed from Google Play. Developer options need not stay on after enabling. Sources: https://www.androidauthority.com/google-android-advanced-flow-sideloading-rollout-begins-3700073/, https://support.google.com/android/answer/17065026?hl=en and https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/faq

A cheap CI guard is available. The Android Developer ID Status API (androiddeveloperidstatus.googleapis.com, API key, 1,000 requests per day) can check whether io.github.nauroth.rouxtine is registered and whether it matches the project's certificate fingerprint (REGISTERED_WITH_ANOTHER_CERTIFICATE_FINGERPRINT). Later F-Droid or IzzyOnDroid distribution affects registration. If a repository re-signs the app, as F-Droid does without reproducible builds, its key must be added to the registration. If the repository build reaches 50 or more installs before that key is registered, ownership must be proven by publishing a version with assets/adi-registration.properties. A repository using the developer's own key needs no extra step. Source: https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/open-source-app-registration

Firebase specifics that affect a dev channel. The CLI's binary_download_uri 'expires after one hour'. Tester invitations expire after 30 days, and a build shows an expiry notice 30 days before its 150-day limit. Source: https://firebase.google.com/docs/app-distribution/android/distribute-cli
